Muon on the conv filters (+1.3 pp at 9 epochs, E014) took it from ~9 SGD epochs (8.09 s) to ~6.5 Muon epochs (5.89 s, E034). Lookahead has been in the recipe since E001: it is worth ~1 pp (E008/E020) but did not move the knee. Inherited scalar hyperparameters sit on a plateau: LS 0.1-0.3, Muon lr 0.16-0.24, momentum 0.6-0.8, Muon warmup, lr floor near 0.07x. Structural changes to the update move accuracy by ~1 pp: Muon +1.3, Muon-C -1.2, lookahead +-1. The update-side levers left are structural: batch size / step count (H1.2.3), how strongly NS orthogonalizes over training, the head's update (the head lr is sensitive, E039), and augmentation. Next target: <=5.6 s.

updates.reason: D009-D011 point both ways. Muon and momentum methods tolerate a larger critical batch (C0106/C0118/C0138), but critical batch grows with horizon and data, and ~320 steps is a small-CBS regime (C0110/C0131). The break-even is tight: the step overhead removed is ~3%, plus 1-2% from larger GEMMs, while the tip's margin is only 0.21 pp. Search: Hiverge (1536) and airbench94_muon (2000) both run Muon at larger batch, but without lookahead. Confidence lowered slightly; scaling rules and pre-registration made concrete. Still the largest untried lever.

Search: the only speedrun evidence (airbench96_faster, -21%) is at 45 epochs with TTA. Keller left it out of the ~8-epoch airbench94_muon record. At ~6.5 epochs each image is seen only ~6 times, so dropping half the backprop samples probably costs more accuracy than it saves. Kept as low-priority.
Selective-Backprop has CIFAR-100 precedent, but only against slow long-horizon SGD baselines. Not a priority next to batch size and resolution.

E029 (Muon: 640-wide block 3, +0.34 pp for +5.5% time = 0.062 pp per 1%) is indistinguishable from the Muon epoch rate (~0.076 pp per 1%, 6.5->7), as H1.5 says ('about the same rate'). The E029 note's 'half the epoch rate / local optimum' overreaches (review). Slope errors are about +-30-50%, so this is not established.
SGD-era prediction framed against the 8.09 s tip. E011 (SGD) and E029 (Muon) together cover it. H1.5.2 is the time-matched test on the current base.
Still the deciding time-matched width test (review). Expected outcome under H5 is within +-0.2 pp, so it is low priority unless the H5 band needs a check.

updates.statement: With lookahead heavily weighting late iterates, the end of training matters through what it feeds the average. A non-zero tail lr supplies diverse iterates: decay-to-0 hurt (E025 -0.51 pp Muon; E012 -0.23 pp SGD, bundled with a warmup change). A higher Muon floor of 0.15x did not help (E033 -0.17 pp, within noise; it does not show 0.15x is worse). BN recalibration of the averaged weights adds nothing (E035). The averaging-horizon change in E028 matched the old tip to 0.003 pp and may have been a no-op under compile, so 'horizon is flat' is not established.
updates.reason: Rolled up: H1.6.2 refuted (E025), H1.6.4 and H1.6.5 refuted as predictions. E028 is a suspected no-op (review). The only open lever left here is averaging strength/density, which depends on the no-op check.

E028 is inconclusive and may be a no-op (review: identical mean to 0.003 pp; E034 showed compile can silently drop changes). Run the no-op check (new node) before reusing E028. If the change was dropped, retest 0.97^5 and sync every 3 steps.

E033: floor 0.15x gave -0.17 pp against the predicted >=+0.2 pp, so the gain prediction failed by ~0.37 pp. Per the symmetric-noise critique, this does not show the 0.15x floor is worse. Only that it is not a >=0.2 pp lever.
E035: +0.03 pp against >=+0.2 pp predicted, at +4.8% time (partly a warmup-layout leak in trial 0). Lookahead already blends the BN buffers consistently.

updates.statement: On the Muon base, the SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head) still runs settings inherited from CIFAR-10 SGD airbench: lr 9, wd 0.012, BN-bias lr x64. Unlike the Muon scalars, the head lr is not on a plateau: halving it cost 0.41 pp (E039). So the 100-way head may be under-driven at ~6.5 epochs, and the BN-bias multiplier is untested. LS is flat from 0.1 to 0.3 (E004, E036) and is no longer a lever here.
updates.reason: E039 (head lr x0.5: -0.41 pp) shows sensitivity, and the slope points upward. E036 closes LS. Search: in the CIFAR-10 lineage the effective head lr was not raised for Muon (airbench94 ~0.0185, airbench94_muon ~0.020, Hiverge ~0.013, given assumed loss reductions), so an upward optimum would be CIFAR-100-specific. That is plausible with a 100-way head.

updates.statement: At the tip's epoch count, at least one remaining one-factor change to the SGD group beats the tip's mean accuracy by >=0.25 pp. Candidates: head lr x1.5 or x2 (lr*wd constant), or BN-bias lr multiplier 64 -> 32 or 128. Head lr x0.5 is already ruled out (E039 -0.41 pp).
updates.reason: E039 refuted only the x0.5 candidate. The existential claim still stands for the untested candidates, so the statement now drops x0.5 and the node stays open.
E036: LS 0.1 gave -0.02 pp against the predicted >=+0.2 pp. Together with E004 (SGD), LS is flat from 0.1 to 0.3 in both regimes.

Untested. Search: the airbench paper finds alternating-flip gains shrink at short horizons, and translate was never ablated. Hiverge uses brightness/contrast jitter at ~7.65 epochs. Now that LS is flat, augmentation is the natural complement (review).

updates.statement: Adding per-sample GPU jitter to the Muon tip at its epoch count gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time. Use Hiverge's exact settings, applied in normalized input space inside the compiled augment: inputs += U(-1,1)*0.1399, then inputs *= 1+U(-1,1)*0.1308.
updates.reason: Search gives Hiverge's exact settings and confirms the jitter is applied after normalization.

updates.statement: With the recipe and epochs held fixed, per-step GPU work can still be cut by a few percent at unchanged accuracy. The cuts must remove GPU work, not launches: E005, E038 and Fable's CUDA-graph result show launch overhead is hidden at bs >=1024. Keeps so far total ~11%: E007 ~1% (possibly jitter), E010 2.0%, E021 2.2%, E023 2.7%, E034 3.0%. Remaining candidates: Muon weight-norm projection frequency, NS iteration count or preconditioning, training the whitening bias for <1 epoch, and the resolution curriculum (H2.3, a FLOP cut that trades some accuracy). Conv-shape and algorithm-selection levers are <=~1% (E007, E032).
updates.reason: E034 added another 3%. E032 closed the conv-shape lever and E038 the launch lever. Statement updated to the current total and to the remaining GPU-work candidates.

The E010+ token is misfiled: E010 removed an atomic GPU kernel, which is H2.4's mechanism, not launch overhead. Refutation is confirmed by E005 and E038, and independently by Fable's CUDA-graph result (0.04 s slower).

Raised. The E013 post-mortem compared its 0.058 pp per 1% against a wrong epoch rate (0.18; the correct value is 0.096 pp per 1%, E015). On SGD, low-res epochs were therefore the cheapest trade measured (review). Fable's CIFAR-10 record gets ~10.6% time from a bilinear whole-image 24->28->32 curriculum with epochs added; the 28->32 stage alone gave ~6.5%.

SGD-base prediction, superseded by H2.3.2 and the new 28->32 node on the Muon base. With corrected arithmetic, E013 was a favourable trade that was never compensated with extra epochs, so the close-out was wrong. The node is retired as stale, not refuted.

Fable's recipe supports the design: bilinear whole images, a true global pool, about +18% epochs, about -10.6% time. Note: the tip's F.max_pool2d(x,4) head assumes a 4x4 final map. Under the unpadded 2x2 whitening, 24 px gives a 2x2 map, so the head must become a global max. Check it with debug_nan because of the E009 amax-backward bug.

updates.statement: Non-conv work that takes a visible share of GPU time can be cut with no change to accuracy by doing less of it. Four instances so far: the atomic adaptive-pool backward (E010, -2.0%), GELU -> SiLU (E021, -2.2%), a batched compiled Muon step (E023, -2.7%), and freezing the whitening bias after epoch 1 so block 1's first-conv dgrad is skipped (E034, -3.0%). The remaining Muon cost (~1.4 ms/step) is GPU kernel time, not launch gaps (E038). Candidates left: weight-norm projection frequency (H2.4.3), fewer or preconditioned NS iterations, and training the whitening bias for 0.2 epoch (~0.5%, below jitter).
updates.reason: E034 supports the mechanism (fourth instance). E038 locates the remaining Muon cost in GPU work.
E034: -3.0% time (5.894 vs 6.077 s), accuracy +0.05 pp. Prediction met (>=2%, within +-0.2 pp).

E038 shows the Muon cost is real GPU work, part of it norms and projection. Hiverge's code confirms the norm_freq = 2+int(15*progress) schedule. Measure the projection's share with drafts/time_muon.py first; if the predicted saving is <1.5%, a single run cannot resolve it.
E038: -0.15% time, far below the 3% predicted. Fable found the same with a whole-run CUDA graph (0.04 s slower).

updates.statement: Conv algorithm selection and conv shapes are not where time goes. Odd spatial sizes cost almost nothing (E032), and max-autotune/cudnn.benchmark gained ~1.1% at most (E007, within jitter). The E007 settings carry costs: a 77 s build, the E035 trial-0 autotune leak, and kernel choices tuned on SXM that may not transfer to the PCIe judge. Whether they are worth keeping is unmeasured.
updates.reason: E032 refuted the shape mechanism (H2.5.2). Restated around the open E007-keep question (H2.5.1), which the review flags as cheap and as a judge-transfer risk.
E032: slicing the whitening output to 30x30 gave -0.1% time (predicted >=3%), accuracy -0.03 pp.
Evidence: E001 (prepare 0.06-0.15 s, <2% of time) and the E003 profile (augment plus gather ~0.16 s/run; the step is GPU-bound).

Evidence: the E003 profile showed flat per-step time over 8x48 steps. E035 showed what breaks it: a warmup tensor in the wrong memory layout (NCHW instead of channels_last) leaked +0.6 s of autotuning into trial 0. Warmups must match the timed path's shape and layout, and trial-0 vs later-trial times should be compared.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the local 0.753 gate on fixed seeds 0-2, not the official 40-seed 0.75 bar. The tip's margin is 0.21 pp, partly built on small keeps (E024 +0.17, E026 +0.18) and on an epoch choice (E027, 6.5 epochs) that bent its own pre-registered rule. How much a code change re-draws the 3-seed mean is now uncertain: ~0.15 pp sd on the SGD base, apparently much less on the current Muon base. Measuring that noise, and the tip's extra-seed margin, decides how close to the knee the recipe can safely run.
updates.reason: Review: the noise model is contradicted on the Muon base, verdicts were asymmetric, and E027 deviated from its pre-registration. The Lvl1 claim stands, but it now depends on re-measuring noise.

updates.statement: A bit-identical commit reruns deterministically in accuracy, with ~1% timing jitter (E003). On the SGD base and the first Muon commits, edits moved the 3-seed mean by up to ~0.18 pp (E005 -0.18, E010 +0.09, E023 -0.14). On the current Muon base, seven consecutive small edits moved it by <=0.06 pp (E028, E031, E032, E034, E035, E036, E038), three of them changing the math from step 0 (E031, E032, E036). At sd 0.15 that pattern has probability ~0.03 or less. So either the paired sd on the current base is <=~0.06 pp, or several of these edits barely changed the trajectory. Accuracy deltas of ~0.15-0.25 pp cannot be graded until the noise is re-measured.
updates.reason: Review: the old sd ~0.15 pp contradicts the recent run of tiny deltas. Downgraded from supported to inconclusive. Verdicts of 0.15-0.25 pp since E024 (E024, E026, E033, E037) carry this uncertainty.

E020 adds the Muon case: removing lookahead costs ~0.9 pp with Muon, against ~1.0 pp with SGD (E008). The airbench paper reports lookahead saves ~1.2 of ~10 epochs on CIFAR-10, a smaller relative effect.

updates.statement: On the Muon base, with optimizer and averaging fixed, no reallocation of FLOPs across width, depth or resolution beats changing the epoch count by more than ~0.03 pp per 1% of time. The Muon epoch rate is ~0.08 pp per 1% of time (slope ~0.9+-0.3 pp/epoch at 6.5-7 epochs). Evidence: E029 width 0.062 pp per 1%; E037 block-1 depth worse than epochs under Muon. The test most likely to break this band is the bilinear resolution curriculum (H2.3.2 / 28->32). On SGD, low-res epochs priced at 0.058 against 0.096 pp per 1% for epochs (E013 with corrected arithmetic), which is just past the band.
updates.reason: Review: the old 0.05-0.13 range was too wide to falsify. Restated as a band, with its error bars and the counterexample most likely to break it. The 'steepening' slope claims are single-run differences, so the slope is treated as 0.9+-0.3 pp/epoch.
E037: on the Muon base, cutting block-1 depth and adding 0.5 epoch at matched time gave -0.24 pp. The SGD-era finding (E015) does not carry over. Muon appears to use depth more efficiently.
E037: -0.24 pp against the predicted >=+0.2 pp, so the prediction missed by ~0.44 pp.

new.statement: On the tip, three numerically different but math-neutral edits and one RNG-shifting edit each move the 3-seed mean by <=0.08 pp. Example neutral edits: NS accumulation in fp32 vs bf16, reordered foreach updates, a different but equivalent lookahead blend expression. Example RNG-shifting edit: one dummy torch.randn in prepare before the permutations. This means the paired sd on the Muon base is <=~0.06 pp. The RNG-shifting edit moves the mean more than the RNG-preserving ones. Run offline in drafts/ where possible.

The E028 lookahead change (base decay 0.95^5 -> 0.97^5) did not take effect in the timed path, for example because a schedule constant was captured at compile time or the alpha schedule is built elsewhere. Check in drafts/: log the per-sync alpha the tip actually applies at a few steps and compare the final seed-0 weights of the E027 and E028 commits. Supported if the alphas match the 0.95^5 schedule or the weights are identical.

How strongly Muon orthogonalizes should be scheduled over training. Scale the momentum matrix fed to NS3 to a Frobenius norm below 1. Three quintic iterations then saturate only the large singular directions, which gives smaller, less whitened updates late in training. This damps late noise without removing the tail lr, which decay-to-0 did and which hurt (E025). Hiverge does this on its CIFAR-10 Muon record.

On the tip at 6.5 epochs, rescale each momentum matrix before NS3 to a Frobenius norm that decays linearly from 0.50 to 0.08 over training, instead of normalizing to 1. Weight-norm projection, the lr schedule and everything else stay unchanged. This gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time. Risk: smaller updates act like a Muon lr below 0.16, which has never been tested.

On the tip at 6.5 epochs, doubling the head lr in the SGD group, with lr*wd held constant (wd halved), gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time. E039 showed halving it cost 0.41 pp. If x2 overshoots, x1.5 is the follow-up.

On the Muon tip, train the first 3 epochs on bilinearly downsampled 28 px whole images and the rest at 32 px, raising total epochs from 6.5 to ~7.0 with schedules scaled to the step count. This reaches >=0.753 at >=3% less time than the tip. Requirements: replace the max_pool2d(x,4) head with a global max over the final map and check it with debug_nan (E009 amax bug); compile and warm up both resolutions and the partial batch in build() with channels_last tensors. This is the safer first step before the 24->28->32 schedule (H2.3.2): in Fable's CIFAR-10 ablation the 28->32 stage gave most of the saving.

Cutting NS from 3 iterations to 2 saves >=0.25 ms/step of Muon GPU time (measured with drafts/time_muon.py) and >=1.2% mean time, with mean accuracy within +-0.15 pp of the tip. Use Turbo-Muon's AOL preconditioning: rescale X0 by diag(row sums of |X0^T X0|)^-1/2, reusing the first Gram matrix. E017 showed NS5 -> NS3 cost nothing, so the iteration axis has not reached its floor.

structured_output.summary:
I rewrote H1 around one pattern. Only structural changes to the update move accuracy by ~1 pp: Muon, Muon-C and lookahead. Inherited scalar settings (LS, Muon lr and momentum, warmup, lr floor) sit on a plateau. The knee shift is now credited to Muon, not lookahead, which was in the recipe from E001.

Node statuses are synced with their verdicts:
- **Refuted:** H1.6.4, H1.6.5, H1.7.2, H2.4.4, H2.5.2, H5.1 and H5.1.1.
- **Supported:** H2.4.2 (E034).
- **Retired:** H1.5.1 and H2.3.1, as stale SGD-era predictions.
- **Rescoped, still open:** H1.7.1 now excludes head lr x0.5.
- **Evidence refiled:** E010 belongs to H2.4, E030 refutes only Muon-C, E012 belongs to H1.6, and H3.1/H3.2 now cite E001, E003 and E035.

The noise model H4.1 drops to inconclusive. Seven recent edits on the Muon base moved the mean by at most 0.06 pp, which contradicts the assumed ~0.15 pp sd. New node N1 re-measures it. N2 tests whether E028 (the lookahead horizon change) was a no-op, so H1.6 no longer claims the horizon is flat.

H2.3 goes up after the E013 arithmetic was corrected and Fable's curriculum results came in. New node N5 tests a 28→32 px curriculum on the Muon tip. H5 is restated as a falsifiable band, with the resolution curriculum as the test most likely to break it.

H1.2.3 (bs 1536) is updated with concrete scaling rules, a drafts timing gate and pre-registered thresholds; its confidence is slightly lower because the literature points both ways. Other new nodes: N3/N3a (Hiverge's scheduled partial orthogonalization), N4 (head lr x2, the direction E039 suggests) and N6 (NS2 with Turbo-Muon preconditioning).

Recommended order:
1. N2 (E028 no-op check), then N1 (noise), both cheap and in drafts.
2. H1.2.3 (bs 1536).
3. N5 (28→32 curriculum).
4. N4 (head lr x2).
5. H2.4.3 (projection every k steps).
6. H1.8.1 (jitter) and N3a (partial orthogonalization).
